br.note: Liam Neeson's Highlander and Tim Roth's foppish villain
Robert the Bruce, the sequel Braveheart never got
Branagh's Agincourt

DiCaprio, the bear, the cold

core.t: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World

Hopkins as Bligh, Mel Gibson as Christian

br.note: Dustin Hoffman, 121 years old, remembers Custer

Mel Gibson and Sigourney Weaver in Jakarta, 1965

Zhang Yimou's palace of gold and poison
Indian mythic spectacle. RRR's big brother

br.note: Cimino's notorious western epic. Beyond the final boss on Westerns

Nigel Hawthorne's mad king

Christian Bale's Moses. Bad

The first CinemaScope film

br.t: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ
br.note: The silent original: the chariot race is even wilder

br.note: Bondarchuk's battle with real armies. Also on War
Ridley Scott, Joaquin Phoenix. Poor man's Gladiator

br.note: Malick's wheat fields at magic hour

br.note: Lean's last film
Denzel Washington, Spike Lee

br.note: Scorsese's Jesuits in 17th-century Japan

br.note: Also on World cinema

core.b: David Lean's Russian Revolution: Omar Sharif, Julie Christie, the ice palace and Lara's theme.

br.note: Lean's Irish storm-and-scandal epic
Desert, burns and a cave of swimmers

Heston's Gordon, Olivier's Mahdi

core.b: Scorsese's Osage murders: oil money, a slow conspiracy and DiCaprio's dimwit husband. Three and a half hours.
Paul Thomas Anderson: Daniel Day-Lewis's oilman Daniel Plainview, a preacher, and the milkshake. A towering performance.

br.note: Nolan's atomic biopic

br.note: A thief impersonates a dead warlord. Palme d'Or
Core on Action and Asian action

core.b: Warren Beatty's John Reed and Diane Keaton's Louise Bryant in the Russian Revolution, with real witnesses between scenes. Long, earnest, on AFI's epic top 10.

br.note: Bertolucci's five-hour Italian century

core.b: Visconti: Burt Lancaster's Sicilian prince watches his world end in the 1860s, culminating in a 45-minute ball. Sumptuous and elegiac.

br.note: Visconti's Venice in 1866
Scorsese's gilded New York

beyond.b: Sergei Bondarchuk's seven-hour Tolstoy, made with the Soviet army: the biggest battle scenes ever filmed, and a ballroom to match.
Abel Gance's silent five-and-a-half-hour biopic, with the triple-screen finale that invented widescreen 30 years early.
beyond.w: Silent, five and a half hours.
